message.content:
The bull case rests on a record third quarter in which revenue reached $1.85 billion, up 36.54% from a year earlier, and net income reached $397 million, up 107.85%, with revenue up 7.51% on the quarter before [D1]. Segment operating income rose 81.36% to $613 million, with the Communications Solutions Group growing revenue 43.09% to $1.345 billion and operating income 86.18% to $458 million, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group growing revenue 21.60% to $501 million and operating income 68.48% to $155 million [D1]. Management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, which is 37% growth at the mid-point, and to non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on roughly 172 million diluted shares [D1]. On the call the company said wireline delivered record orders that more than doubled from a year earlier and that demand was far exceeding its ability to supply [D3]. Management expects the 6G opportunity to be larger than the 5G cycle and described its rolling 12-month funnel as being at an all-time high [D4]. The bull case needs to see fourth quarter revenue at or above $1.95 billion and earnings per share at or above $3.40 [D1]. It also needs orders to rise again from the third quarter with the funnel still at a record [D4].

The bear case rests on supply rather than demand, since management called the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue and said the supply environment was less flexible than a year earlier [D3]. The fourth quarter revenue guide of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion is only a modest step up from third quarter revenue of $1.85 billion, and analysts pressed management on whether supply, not demand, was capping the outlook [D3]. The chief financial officer warned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 artificially lifted profitability and will not repeat, which sets a high comparison bar [D3]. Costs still rose, with cost of products and services up 21.62% to $630 million, research and development up 23.75% to $312 million and selling, general and administrative expense up 25.99% to $446 million [D1]. Management said revenue conversion would be nonlinear over the next several quarters while it manages external component supply [D4]. One commentary cautions that analyst price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide them, which tempers the upside implied by sell-side targets [D5]. The bear case needs to see revenue conversion still governed by supply and fourth quarter revenue at or below $1.93 billion with earnings per share at or below $3.34 [D1].
